```lean
import Mathlib

open Nat

theorem rmo_2001_2 (p q : ℕ) (hp : Nat.Prime p) (hq : Nat.Prime q) :
  (∃ m : ℕ, p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2) ↔
    (p = q ∨ (p = 3 ∧ q = 11) ∨ (p = 11 ∧ q = 3)) := by
  constructor
  · intro h
    -- If p = q, then p² + 7pq + q² = 9p² = (3p)², so it's a perfect square
    -- We need to show that if there exists m such that p² + 7pq + q² = m²,
    -- then either p = q or {p,q} = {3,11}
    rcases h with ⟨m, hm⟩
    have h₁ : p ≤ m := by
      nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
    have h₂ : q ≤ m := by
      nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
    -- Consider the difference m² - (p+q)² = 5pq
    -- This gives us (m-(p+q))(m+(p+q)) = 5pq
    -- Since p and q are primes, we analyze the factorization
    have h₃ : p = q ∨ p = 3 ∧ q = 11 ∨ p = 11 ∧ q = 3 := by
      by_cases h_eq : p = q
      · exact Or.inl h_eq
      -- If p ≠ q, WLOG assume p < q
      have h_neq : p ≠ q := h_eq
      have h_lt : p < q ∨ q < p := by
        cases' lt_or_gt_of_ne h_neq with hlt hgt
        · exact Or.inl hlt
        · exact Or.inr hgt
      cases' h_lt with h_lt h_lt
      · -- Case p < q
        -- We use the fact that (p+q)² < p² + 7pq + q² < (p+4q)² for large enough q
        -- More precisely, we check that m must satisfy certain bounds
        have h_bound : m < p + 4*q := by
          nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
        have h_bound2 : m > p + q := by
          nlinarith [Nat.Prime.two_le hp, Nat.Prime.two_le hq]
        -- Now we know p+q < m < p+4q
        -- We can enumerate possible values of m and check which work
        have h_case : p = 3 ∧ q = 11 := by
          -- For p=3, q=11: 9 + 231 + 121 = 361 = 19² ✓
          -- We verify this is the only solution with p < q
          have h_p_ge : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hp
          have h_q_ge : q ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hq
          -- Check small values of p
          interval_cases p <;> 
            (try contradiction) <;>
            (try {
              have h_q_prime : Nat.Prime q := hq
              have h_q_ge_3 : q ≥ 3 := by
                by_contra h
                have : q ≤ 2 := by linarith
                have : q = 2 := by omega
                simp_all [Nat.Prime]
              -- For each p, check possible q values
              have h_q_bound : q ≤ 100 := by
                by_contra h
                have : q ≥ 101 := by omega
                have : p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 > (p + 4*q)^2 := by
                  nlinarith
                linarith
              interval_cases q <;> norm_num at hq ⊢ <;>
                (try contradiction) <;>
                (try {
                  have : p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2 := hm
                  norm_num at this
                  omega
                })
            })
          <;> simp_all
        exact Or.inr (Or.inl h_case)
      · -- Case q < p
        -- Symmetric to the previous case
        have h_case : p = 11 ∧ q = 3 := by
          have h_p_ge : p ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hp
          have h_q_ge : q ≥ 2 := Nat.Prime.two_le hq
          interval_cases q <;>
            (try contradiction) <;>
            (try {
              have h_p_prime : Nat.Prime p := hp
              have h_p_ge_3 : p ≥ 3 := by
                by_contra h
                have : p ≤ 2 := by linarith
                have : p = 2 := by omega
                simp_all [Nat.Prime]
              have h_p_bound : p ≤ 100 := by
                by_contra h
                have : p ≥ 101 := by omega
                have : p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 > (p + 4*q)^2 := by
                  nlinarith
                linarith
              interval_cases p <;> norm_num at hp ⊢ <;>
                (try contradiction) <;>
                (try {
                  have : p^2 + 7*p*q + q^2 = m^2 := hm
                  norm_num at this
                  omega
                })
            })
          <;> simp_all
        exact Or.inr (Or.inr h_case)
    exact h₃
  · intro h
    rcases h with (h | h | h)
    · -- Case p = q
      -- Then p² + 7pq + q² = p² + 7p² + p² = 9p² = (3p)²
      refine ⟨3*p, _⟩
      rw [h]
      ring
    · -- Case p = 3, q = 11
      -- Then 9 + 231 + 121 = 361 = 19²
      refine ⟨19, _⟩
      rw [h]
      norm_num
    · -- Case p = 11, q = 3
      -- Then 121 + 231 + 9 = 361 = 19²
      refine ⟨19, _⟩
      rw [h]
      norm_num
